findings: C is the key: "the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything" - the number is the gas-in-air share at first detection.

A dies on "three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow": the figure RISES as the warning weakens, and since "He is working to four", eleven is a bad figure, not a good one.
B dies on "The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air": the quarter-turns are how he opens the valve, not what he records.
D dies on "opens its needle valve a quarter-turn at a time and sniffs at the funnel until the smell arrives": the figure is measured at the nose, not computed from pipe length.
justification: Arithmetic check: target four parts per thousand = 0.4 percent, and "a fifth of the leanest mixture of propane and air that will burn" (propane LFL 2.1 percent) gives 0.42 percent - the figures reconcile.

findings: A is the key: "Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells" - partly changed into a compound the nose can hardly pick up.
B dies on "put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume".

C dies on the timing: the oxide is already there before service - "a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard" - and "Bare oxide takes the most, so a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service", i.e. the taking is greatest at the start and stops with age, not once corrosion begins in service.
D dies on "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in": the loss is in the pipe, not at the cooker.
justification: Only A matches the two stated fates of the mercaptan (sticking and oxidation to a near-odourless disulphide); C inverts the passage's age relation.

findings: D is the key: "Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged" plus "reads three at both ends" for a line in service "since the sixties".
A dies on "is longer than the new run".
B dies on "is the same bore".
C dies on "comes off the same vessel and the same fill".
justification: The passage deliberately equalises length, bore, vessel and fill so that only saturation with age explains the flat three-to-three reading.

findings: B is the key by both support and elimination: "The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again", and the closing walk (figure six, against a target of four) shows the criterion is a re-walk, not a calendar date.
A dies twice: "holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose" (not the ordinary dose) and "What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance".
C dies on "costs more than the odorant does": one call-out outweighs the odorant, so the odorant is not the main cost.
D dies on "and you do it before the first burner is lit".
justification: B's wording about a second walk of the run is looser than "walking the run again", but the ending criterion it states is the passage's own and the other three options are each contradicted outright, so B stands.

findings: D is the key: "every joint was pressure-tested, the paperwork is signed" yet eleven parts per thousand are needed before the smell arrives, and "The slope is not a fault in the pipe and it is not a fault in the fill".
A dies on "it is not a fault in the fill" plus "put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume".
B dies on "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in": the warning does not survive the run.
C dies on "The pipe that needs watching is the pipe nobody has ever used" and "a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service".
justification: The whole piece is built on a clean-tested new main delivering under-odorised gas, which is exactly D.

findings: D (Worse) is the key: the gap sits at the top of an escalating indictment - "for eight minutes none of the three adults living there could turn the water off", then "none could say which side of the path", then a tenure that is "long enough to have asked" - and a bare Worse ranks an additional aggravating fact.
A (Nowadays) dies on "There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either": no then-versus-now contrast is in play.
C (Happily) dies on polarity - "The hall carpet took most of the damage".

B (Oddly) is the near miss and the reason this gap is not a walkover: as a disjunct it would predicate oddness of the residence itself, whereas the clause "which is long enough to have asked" supplies a reproach, i.e. a ranking of badness rather than a surprise.
justification: Closest call of the three sentence-adverb gaps; Worse fits the escalation and the scope of the following relative clause, Oddly misattaches.

findings: A (witness) is the key: the apposition defines it - "somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since" - and the next paragraph repeats "by being in the room when it happens".
B (recruit) dies on "This competence is not earned and not handed out": nobody is enlisted.
C (caretaker) dies on "The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house".
D (lodger) dies on "It may sit with the owner, the owner’s daughter, or the man who rents the back bedroom": the lodger is one possible holder, not the category.
justification: The gloss after the colon is a definition of witness - presence, not appointment.

findings: B (caught) is the key: "the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens" - colds are caught.
A (issued) dies on "This competence is not earned and not handed out".
C (bought) dies on "The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house".
D (chosen) dies on "Nobody else will have it, because there is nothing in it to have": no selection is involved.
justification: The simile fixes the verb: contagion, not issue, purchase or choice.

findings: A (address) is my answer: every predicate in the gloss takes a designating expression as subject - "It names one thing in one building and explains nothing; most are four words long; nobody disputes them" - and “the one behind the coats” is exactly an address for a valve, valid in one building only.

B (instance) is the reason this line is flagged rather than passed clean: it is defensible against "no rule, no principle" read as the general-versus-particular contrast, but an instance does not "name" and is not "four words long", and an instance presupposes the general the passage has just denied.
C (opinion) dies on "nobody disputes them".
D (anecdote) dies on "most are four words long" and "explains nothing": four words is no anecdote.
justification: Narrowest margin in the unit; A wins on the predicate-type test (names / word length / undisputed) but B survives a general-versus-particular reading well enough to be worth the resolver's attention.

findings: C (commonplace) is the key: the concession needs a property that ought to make the knowledge spread easily - "Nothing on that list is difficult and nothing on it is being kept back. Ask, and you will be told gladly and at length, and still have nothing".
A (privileged) dies on "nothing on it is being kept back".
B (perishable) breaks the concession: perishability is another reason it fails to travel, not something "Although" can concede against one-way transmission.
D (technical) dies on "Nothing on that list is difficult".
justification: Although-clause demands an ordinariness concession, which only commonplace supplies.

findings: D is the key and is quoted outright: "The last octave comes in over somebody’s left hand, two octaves down, and that’s what it has to agree with".
A dies on "she played a dozen notes into her meter, the last of them from the top octave" and on the curve covering "all eighty-eight notes": the sample reaches the top and the curve does not stop.
B dies on "this upright’s figure is larger than a grand’s, its short thick strings already counted in it": the small instrument's stiffness is already in the figure.
C dies on "The extra cents are not an allowance for the cold".
justification: Physics reconciles: the fourth partial is two octaves above the fundamental, so "A note down in the tenor has its fourth partial about nine cents sharp" and the treble note two octaves up landing nine cents wide are the same fact.

findings: A is the key: every day on the card is that town's market day - "Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long" and "Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday".
B dies on "The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use": a place off the road is still on the card, so the road did not settle inclusion.
C dies on "Upper Shenwold has no market of its own".
D dies on "the Thursday market is the largest of the four".
justification: Mileage reconciles and supports A: Nerresby is nine miles from Haddenthorpe and "Thrapmere stands thirty miles from Nerresby, and the road to it runs back through Haddenthorpe and twenty-one miles beyond" (9 + 21 = 30), so the Tuesday-to-Wednesday leg doubles back - an order no route-planner would choose, and the 1227 charter predates the 1769 turnpike by five centuries.

findings: B är nyckeln: "Den översta bokstaven är 73 millimeter, nästa rad 36" och "Det första steget halverar alltså bokstavshöjden" - 37 mm är det största steget, både absolut och relativt.
A dör på "Storlekarna följer ingen jämn trappa".
C dör på "mellan de två nedersta raderna skiljer det åtta tiondels millimeter" - 0,8 mm mot 37 mm högst upp.
D dör på "Sedan blir stegen kortare": stegen krymper hela vägen nedåt, så mitten är aldrig störst.
justification: Siffrorna går ihop: 73 till 36 är en halvering, och 0,8 mm på en rad som är "drygt sju millimeter" hög är ungefär en tiondel, precis som texten säger.

findings: C är nyckeln: "beror inte på hur många millimeter som skiljer tecknen åt, utan på hur stort det avståndet är i förhållande till tecknet självt".
A dör på "Två små bokstäver med ett litet mellanrum trängs lika mycket som två stora med ett stort".
B dör på "Den sitter inte i ögats upplösning: näthinnan skiljer ut tecknet".
D dör på "Trängseln växer alltså nedåt på arket i takt med att bokstäverna krymper" - den avtar inte.
justification: Texten definierar trängsel som ett förhållande, inte ett millimetertal, och D är en ren riktningsvändning.

findings: D är nyckeln: "Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid, utan de sjuttio tecknen: var och en ska höras och prickas av".
A dör på "Ingen rad prövas om".
B dör på samma mening: "Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid".
C dör på "Även ett barn som stannar högt upp tar längre tid än förut" - fördröjningen sitter inte längst ned.
justification: Tidsangivelserna går ihop: fyrtio barn på två timmar är tre minuter styck, och 120 minuter delat på sju ger sjutton barn.

findings: A är nyckeln: "Nedgången i kurvan ligger på det året" och "utan mellan två på varandra följande årgångar", med bytet "under höstterminen 1978".
B dör på "de mäter alltså inte samma sak" och "Som en enda kurva över barns syn i en svensk stad går den inte att läsa".
C dör på "Gränsen 0,8 ändrades inte vid bytet".
D dör på "samma steg finns i de tre distriktens siffror var för sig".
justification: Årtalen går ihop: 1961-1996 är trettiosex årgångar, sjutton före bytet (1961-1977) och nitton efter (1978-1996), vilket lägger brottet exakt vid höstterminen 1978.

findings: D är nyckeln: "Jag begär något annat: att stämman beslutar två saker i samma beslut" - först uttagen, "Sedan i vilken ordning bilarna får ström de nätter då sju är fullt".
A dör på "Delar vi fyrtiofem lika på tio bilar blir det fyra och en halv på var, och då laddar ingen av de tio".
B dör på "Någon större huvudsäkring tänker jag därför inte begära i år".
C dör på "Att den ska stå skriven innan uttagen sitter uppe är däremot hela min poäng" - turordningen får inte skjutas till när den behövs.
justification: Amperetalen går ihop: 125 minus 80 ger 45, 45 delat på 6 ger 7,5 alltså sju bilar, och fyra stolpar à 32 ampere behöver 128 - därför är de snabba bara när tre står tomma.

findings: C är nyckeln: "styrelsens förslag står där som punkt sju".
A dör på "Kallelsen sitter med häftstift på anslagstavlan utanför tvättstugan".
B dör på "Punkten är en rad lång".
D dör på "Var de ska stå framgår inte".
justification: Alla tre felaktiga alternativ motsägs direkt av detaljer i samma stycke.

findings: D är nyckeln: "det skymmer inte sikten. Från gräset utanför ser man golvet från kant till kant", och räcket är "i knähöjd".
A dör på "inte byggt för att hålla någon ute".
B dör på "Räcket är det ursprungliga" med "Börje Ängman, 1934" skåret i virket.
C dör på "Insidan har sin gamla gröna färg i behåll".
justification: Räckets låga höjd bär hela textens poäng om offentlighet, och de tre andra alternativen motsägs var för sig.

findings: A är nyckeln: "Paret som kommer i fart mot ett hörn måste vrida nittio grader på två steg, eller stanna", medan "En rund bana har ingen sådan punkt" och "Den var lättare att gå runt i".
B dör på "utan tak och utan stolpar inne på golvet".
C dör på "Spelmännen satt på en låg scen vid ena kanten" och "längst bort på banan hördes de sämre" - avståndet är inte lika.
D dör på "Golvet ligger plant på sina syllar, och regnet rinner ner mellan brädorna".
justification: Texten avvisar uttryckligen billighetsförklaringen - "Rundningen var inte det billiga valet" - och lägger skälet i rörelsen runt varvet.

findings: Killed on quoted span: the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything
Killed on quoted span: The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air
Killed on quoted span: opens its needle valve a quarter-turn at a time and sniffs at the funnel until the smell arrives
Killed on quoted span: three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow
Killed on quoted span: The box is honest about the dilution and silent about the nose
Gradient is monotonic with distance from the vessel and reconciles with the stated mechanism: 3 at the nearest cottage, 5 halfway, 11 at the far bungalow.
justification: C is the definition given verbatim: “The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air: the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything”. A inverts the gradient: the sheet reads “three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow”, so the figures RISE as the warning weakens, and eleven is the worst reading on the run rather than a good one. B mistakes the method for the datum; the quarter-turn is how he walks the dilution up, since he “opens its needle valve a quarter-turn at a time and sniffs at the funnel until the smell arrives”, while what is written down is the dilution the box reports. D makes the figure a calculation from pipe length, but it is a nose measurement taken house by house: “The box is honest about the dilution and silent about the nose”. Length explains the slope; it does not produce the number.

findings: Killed on quoted span: Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells
Killed on quoted span: put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume
Killed on quoted span: a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard

Killed on quoted span: Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking

justification: A restates the passage directly: “Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells” - partly changed, and the product is near odourless. B is contradicted by “put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume”. C is the near miss and dies on its time clause: the oxide is already present before service, being “a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard”; the taking is worst at the very start, since “a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service”; and corrosion with age works the other way, because “Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking”. So C's requirement that the steel has begun to corrode in service reverses the passage's own order of events. D is contradicted by “the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in”.

findings: Killed on quoted span: Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged

Killed on quoted span: The old steel line that has fed the farm buildings since the sixties is longer than the new run, is the same bore, comes off the same vessel and the same fill, and reads three at both ends
justification: One sentence kills A, B and C a clause at a time: “The old steel line that has fed the farm buildings since the sixties is longer than the new run, is the same bore, comes off the same vessel and the same fill, and reads three at both ends”. Longer defeats A, the same bore defeats B, the same vessel and fill defeat C. What remains - same bore, same fill, longer, and still reading three at both ends - is explained only by age, under the stated rule “Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged”. That is D.

findings: Killed on quoted span: The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again
Killed on quoted span: holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose until it will take no more
Killed on quoted span: What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance
Killed on quoted span: one call-out to a kitchen where the cooker is off and the smell is only the soak costs more than the odorant does
Killed on quoted span: you do it before the first burner is lit
Killed on quoted span: The figure he writes down is six

Arithmetic reconciles with real combustion data: propane's lower flammable limit is about 2.1 vol% = 21 parts per thousand parts of air, and a fifth of that is 4.2, i.e. the stated working figure of four.
The post-soak re-walk reads six, still above four, so the soak is correctly shown as unfinished; option B's word 'second' is looser than 'walking the run again' but creates no rival answer.
justification: B is the only option not contradicted, and it tracks “The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again”: the end is set by re-measurement, not by a date. A fails twice, against “holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose until it will take no more” and against “What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance”. C inverts the economics: “one call-out to a kitchen where the cooker is off and the smell is only the soak costs more than the odorant does”. D is contradicted by “you do it before the first burner is lit”. Noted but not disqualifying: B's word second is looser than the passage, since the re-walk actually shown ends “The figure he writes down is six”, still above the working figure of four, so the soak is not over and further walks may be needed. Read as another walk, which is what walking the run again means, B stands and no rival option survives.

findings: Killed on quoted span: every joint was pressure-tested, the paperwork is signed
Killed on quoted span: The slope is not a fault in the pipe and it is not a fault in the fill
Killed on quoted span: the further it has travelled against that wall, the less it has
Killed on quoted span: The pipe that needs watching is the pipe nobody has ever used
justification: D is the thesis. The run passed its pipework proof - “every joint was pressure-tested, the paperwork is signed” - and still delivers gas that reads eleven, because “The slope is not a fault in the pipe and it is not a fault in the fill”. That same span kills A: the fill is not short of odorant, and the old line off the same vessel and the same fill reads three at both ends. B puts the failure at the cooker, but the loss accrues along the run, since “the further it has travelled against that wall, the less it has”. C is the exact inversion of “The pipe that needs watching is the pipe nobody has ever used”.

findings: Killed on quoted span: There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either
Killed on quoted span: The hall carpet took most of the damage
Killed on quoted span: which is long enough to have asked
justification: D, Worse, is the escalating sentence adverbial the paragraph needs: the eleven years aggravate the failure, which is why the clause closes “which is long enough to have asked” before the deadpan consequence. One span kills two distractors at once, because the next paragraph opens “There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either”. That denies B, Oddly, since the writer's thesis is that this ignorance is entirely normal rather than strange, and it denies A, Nowadays, since nothing here is modern and no then-and-now contrast is in play. C, Happily, is the wrong polarity against “The hall carpet took most of the damage”.

findings: Killed on quoted span: somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since

justification: The gloss after the colon defines a witness: “somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since”, which is presence plus testimony. C, caretaker, imports a role and is killed by “The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house”. D, lodger, takes one of three listed possibilities for the whole, against “It may sit with the owner, the owner’s daughter, or the man who rents the back bedroom”. B, recruit, implies selection and is killed by “This competence is not earned and not handed out”.

findings: Killed on quoted span: the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens

Killed on quoted span: is not bought with the house
justification: The simile fixes the verb, since a cold is caught and the means is given as “the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens”. A, issued, and D, chosen, are both killed by “This competence is not earned and not handed out”, and C, bought, by “is not bought with the house”. The passage rules out every alternative explicitly, which leaves B alone.

findings: Killed on quoted span: It names one thing in one building and explains nothing; most are four words long; nobody disputes them
Killed on quoted span: there is nothing in it to have: no rule, no principle, nothing that carries to another house
Killed on quoted span: the one behind the coats
justification: The next sentence is a definition of an address: “It names one thing in one building and explains nothing; most are four words long; nobody disputes them”. That is a pure locator, which is exactly what the worked example “the one behind the coats” is, and what the paint marker later makes literal. C, opinion, dies on nobody disputes them. D, anecdote, dies on four words long and on explains nothing, since an anecdote recounts rather than names. B, instance, presupposes a general case to be an instance of, which the preceding clause denies outright: “there is nothing in it to have: no rule, no principle, nothing that carries to another house”.

justification: The concessive needs a property that ought to let the knowledge spread freely, and the preceding sentence supplies it: “Nothing on that list is difficult and nothing on it is being kept back”. Entirely commonplace, and yet it moves one way only. That same span kills D, technical, because nothing is difficult, and A, privileged, because nothing is kept back, which “Ask, and you will be told gladly and at length, and still have nothing” reinforces. B, perishable, fails logically, since perishability would not contrast with one-way transmission, and factually, against “whoever is in the hall then has the fact for good”.

Acoustics check out: the fourth partial is two octaves above the fundamental, so a tenor note whose fourth partial is nine cents sharp does place the treble note two octaves up nine cents wide of the arithmetic.
justification: D is her own stated reason: “The last octave comes in over somebody’s left hand, two octaves down, and that’s what it has to agree with”, a musical requirement the curve cannot know rather than a defect in the wire. A is pre-killed in the second paragraph, since “she played a dozen notes into her meter, the last of them from the top octave”, so the sample does not stop short of the treble. B is killed by “this upright’s figure is larger than a grand’s, its short thick strings already counted in it”, the stiffness being already inside the figure. C is killed outright by “The extra cents are not an allowance for the cold”. The physics also checks, because the fourth partial is two octaves above the fundamental, which is why “A note down in the tenor has its fourth partial about nine cents sharp, and that is where the treble note two octaves above it goes” reconciles.

findings: Killed on quoted span: Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long

Mileages reconcile exactly: 9 miles Haddenthorpe-Nerresby plus 21 miles beyond Haddenthorpe = the stated 30 miles Nerresby-Thrapmere.
Geometry is consistent: the Shenwolds are 4 miles from Haddenthorpe and 3 miles off a road running through Haddenthorpe (3 < 4).
Dates are load-bearing and consistent: the 1227 charter predates the 1769 turnpike by 542 years, which is what licenses A over B.
justification: Every card day lands on a market day. “Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long”, and “Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday”. The 1227 charter predates the turnpike by 542 years, so the market days, not the road, set the order of the week: A. B is the attribution the essay undercuts, since “The circuit has been put down to the coach road, turnpiked in 1769” is reported and then falsified by the Shenwolds appearing on the card even though “The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use”. C is killed by “Upper Shenwold has no market of its own”, the pairing being the ten minute walk rather than two markets. D is killed by “the Thursday market is the largest of the four”. The mileages reconcile: nine miles Haddenthorpe to Nerresby plus twenty-one beyond Haddenthorpe equals the stated thirty to Thrapmere.

findings: Killed on quoted span: Den översta bokstaven är 73 millimeter, nästa rad 36 och den därefter 24.
Killed on quoted span: Det första steget halverar alltså bokstavshöjden, det sista ändrar den med en tiondel.
Killed on quoted span: Storlekarna följer ingen jämn trappa.
Killed on quoted span: mellan de två nedersta raderna skiljer det åtta tiondels millimeter

Den gamla trappan gar ihop med visusidentiteten langre ned: pa 5 m ar 1,0-raden 5 bagminuter = 7,27 mm (drygt sju millimeter), vilket ger 0,1-raden 72,7 (angivet 73), 0,2-raden 36,4 (angivet 36) och 0,3-raden 24,2 (angivet 24); 0,2-raden ar ocksa den som ett normalt oga laser pa 25 m, precis som texten sager.
Forsta steget 73 till 36 ar 37 mm eller 50,7 procent (en halvering); understa steget 0,8 mm pa en rad om 8,07 mm ar 9,9 procent (en tiondel). Bada de angivna karakteristikerna haller.
Bokstavsantalen summerar exakt: 1+2+3+5+6+7+8+8 = 40 pa atta rader, som angivet.

Det nya arkets storleksstege sluter sig exakt pa sin egen identitet: 73 mm overst, faktor 20 over 14 rader ger 73/20 = 3,65 mm (knappt fyra), en radkvot pa 20^(1/13) = 1,259 (ungefar en fjardedel storre), och 7,27/3,65 = 1,99 alltsa visus 2,0.
